title: Best AI Agents for Orthopedics: September 2026
summary: Best AI agents for orthopedic practices compared on prior auth, outbound payer calling, and billing. Only 1 vendor resolves 60%+ of calls end-to-end.
body_markdown:
An AI agent for orthopedic practices is a voice AI system that handles the phone calls an orthopedic front desk fields every day — scheduling, insurance eligibility, prior authorization, and billing — without transferring the caller to staff. The stronger ones also call payers directly when a prior auth needs a live conversation, not just an API check.


Strong scheduling demos are easy to come by in vendor evaluations. What's harder to see in a demo is whether the tool can handle a payer call for surgical prior auth or tell a patient what their injection copay looks like. That gap is what this comparison focuses on.


## **TL;DR**


- Most AI agents for orthopedic practices cover scheduling only, leaving prior auth and billing calls to staff.
- Assess vendors on real-time insurance eligibility, outbound payer calling, and post-launch expandability without re-engineering.
- Scheduling-only tools can cover roughly 40% of your inbound call surface before hitting an architectural ceiling.
- Prosper AI resolves 60%+ of inbound calls end-to-end in production, covering scheduling, prior auth, and billing, based on Prosper AI's customer deployment data.


## What is an AI agent for orthopedic practices?


Orthopedic workflows have a level of complexity that generic call-handling tools struggle with. Injection eligibility windows vary by payer and procedure type. Surgical cases often require[multi-step prior authorization](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prior-authorization-automation-guide) before confirming a date. Implant billing generates inbound calls that need accurate, real-time answers from the patient ledger.


Prior authorization consumes an average of[13 hours of physician and staff time each week](https://www.ama-assn.org/press-center/ama-press-releases/ama-survey-prior-authorization-reform-pledge-falls-short-physicians) , and 94% of physicians say it contributes to burnout. A true AI agent handles these workflows end to end: it reads from and writes back to EHRs like athenahealth, ModMed, and NextGen, calls payers directly when needed, and resolves the call without transferring to staff.


## How we ranked AI agents for orthopedic practices


Picking the right AI agent for an orthopedic practice means looking past demo-day performance. Here are the criteria we weighted in this evaluation:


- Call mix coverage beyond scheduling: can it handle[insurance eligibility lookups](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/real-time-insurance-eligibility-verification-guide) , billing inquiries, and prior authorization follow-ups, or does it stop at the calendar?
- EHR integration depth: does it read from and write back to the EHR, or does staff still enter data manually after the call?
- Resolution rate across the full call surface, beyond scheduling-only containment
- Handling of off-script questions: payer-specific rules, implant billing questions, injection frequency limits
- Multilingual support for patient populations that require it
- Post-launch expandability: can new call types be added through configuration, or does every change require vendor engineering?


We assessed each vendor below against these criteria using publicly available information.


## Best overall AI agent for orthopedic practices: Prosper AI


Prosper AI covers the full administrative call surface orthopedic practices deal with: scheduling, injection eligibility windows, surgical prior authorization, inbound billing inquiries, and outbound payer calls. That last part matters. Prosper AI is the only vendor in this comparison that calls insurance payers directly by phone when API verification falls short, including waiting on payer IVR hold times of 45 to 60 minutes to complete a prior auth.


- Prosper AI resolves 60%+ of all inbound calls end-to-end in production, roughly 2x the rate of scripted workflow tools, per Prosper AI's customer deployment data
- Handles orthopedic-specific workflows: injection eligibility tied to payer rules, surgical prior authorization, and inbound patient billing calls
- Two-stage benefits verification (API-first, phone fallback) with outbound payer calling; no other vendor in this comparison offers this
- 80+ EHR integrations with native read-and-write, including live athenahealth production
- LLM-native (Gen 3) architecture handles off-script questions and mid-call topic changes without resetting the call
- Dedicated AI PM at a 1:5 ratio, biweekly tuning, and initial go-live in approximately 3 weeks, with full production optimization reached over a 10-12 week ramp period
- Multilingual support including Spanish, Mandarin, and Arabic


Prosper AI won a competitive RFP against nine vendors for Spire Orthopedics, including the competitor with the deepest historical build in orthopedics, which is the clearest field validation of its fit for the specialty.


▶[Case Study: How Frederick Foot & Ankle Reduces Scheduling Calls by 70% with Prosper AI](https://www.getprosper.ai/case-study/ai-patient-scheduling-podiatry)


## Assort Health


Assort Health is a scripted agentic state machine built for specialty scheduling, with a deep orthopedic footprint. It routes inbound calls through hardcoded intent nodes, with LLM-generated speech per node in place of LLM orchestration of the full call.


What they offer:


- Inbound scheduling for new and existing orthopedic patients via pre-built specialty nodes
- Deterministic, auditable call flows with predictable per-call cost


It fits single-specialty orthopedic groups whose call volume is largely scheduling with stable, low-variance appointment types and no near-term need for insurance or billing automation.


In a 2026 field evaluation, insurance eligibility lookup and billing calls both returned "No" in the capability matrix, with eligibility handled via a post-call web form instead of real-time verification. Adding call types after go-live requires vendor engineering, not self-configuration, which sets an architectural ceiling of roughly 40% of total inbound call volume.


Practices reviewing[Assort Health alternatives](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/assort-health-alternatives-comparison) may find this ceiling a deciding factor. Practices that need injection eligibility windows, prior authorization, or billing calls covered will need additional vendors to fill that gap.


## Hello Patient


Hello Patient is a multi-channel patient engagement platform covering voice, text, and chat for outpatient practices. Its AI agent, Mia, handles inbound and after-hours calls, two-way text confirmations, digital intake forms, and appointment scheduling.


What they offer:


- AI call agent (Mia) across voice, text, and chat for inbound and after-hours calls
- Two-way text confirmations, digital intake forms, and appointment scheduling and cancellation management


Hello Patient suits outpatient practices that need stronger patient-facing communication across multiple channels but do not require automated insurance verification,[AI patient intake](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/ai-patient-intake-guide-modalities-hipaa-ehr) , or billing call handling.


For orthopedic practices, the gap is RCM depth. For a procedure-heavy specialty with complex payer mixes and[surgical prior auth requirements](https://aaos-annualmeeting-presskit.org/2025/research-news/new-study-shows-prior-authorization-does-not-reduce-costs-for-total-hip-arthroplasty-delays-patient-care/) , that gap is meaningful.


## Hyro


Hyro is a conversational AI agent purpose-built for large health systems, with documented deployment across 45+ health systems. Its agents handle patient scheduling, FAQ answering, provider search, and prescription management across voice, chat, and SMS.


What they offer:


- HIPAA-compliant voice, chat, and SMS agents for patient scheduling, FAQ answering, and provider search across health system deployments
- Conversational AI across multiple patient-facing channels with documented EHR integration


Hyro's depth sits in front-end patient engagement at enterprise scale. The trade-off is scope: payer-facing workflows fall outside what it covers. Staff still handle outbound calls to insurance payers for eligibility verification, prior authorization follow-up, or claims resolution. For an orthopedic group that needs surgical prior auth automated and benefits verification completed without a staff call, that gap is hard to ignore.


The deployment model is also calibrated for enterprise health systems, not mid-size specialty groups. Pricing and implementation reflect that focus, which can make Hyro a poor fit for multi-site orthopedic practices (see the full[Prosper AI vs Hyro](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prosper-ai-vs-hyro-which-is-better) breakdown) that need a vendor sized for specialty care over a 50-hospital footprint.


## Parakeet Health


Parakeet Health is a generative AI voice agent focused on patient engagement and care coordination. Its core workflows cover inbound scheduling, referral conversion, and proactive outbound outreach, including appointment backfilling and care gap closure through automated payer calls to patients.


What they offer:


- Inbound appointment scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellation handling with EHR integration
- Outbound referral follow-up calls to convert referred patients into booked visits
- Proactive appointment backfilling and care gap outreach via voice
- Value-based care workflow support including post-discharge follow-up calls


Parakeet fits organizations whose primary need is referral conversion and outbound patient engagement. For orthopedic practices, the gap is on the payer side. Based on publicly available information, Parakeet has no documented capability for real-time insurance eligibility verification, outbound payer calling, or[AI prior authorization automation](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/ai-prior-authorization-risks-rules-roi) . Those are high-volume workflows in orthopedic settings, particularly for surgical cases. A practice running 30 to 40 surgical prior auths a week still needs staff to handle them.

## Why Prosper AI is the best AI agent for orthopedic practices


Orthopedic practices generate call volume across scheduling, injection eligibility, surgical prior authorization, and billing inquiries. An AI agent that covers scheduling only handles roughly 40% of the inbound surface and leaves the rest to staff. Prosper AI covers all four call types within a single workflow, including outbound payer calling when eligibility or prior auth requires a live phone conversation with the insurer.


The proof is in production. Prosper AI resolves 60%+ of total inbound calls end-to-end per Prosper AI's customer deployment data, roughly twice the rate of scripted scheduling tools. In a competitive RFP against nine vendors for Spire Orthopedics, Prosper AI won outright. For a practice administrator comparing[AI voice agents in healthcare](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/ai-voice-agent-in-healthcare-guide-use-cases) in 2026, those two data points are harder to replicate than any feature list.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do I choose the right AI agent for my orthopedic practice from this list?


Start by mapping your full call mix, including more than scheduling volume. If your practice runs surgical prior authorizations, injection eligibility checks, and inbound billing calls alongside scheduling, you need a vendor whose architecture covers all four. Assort Health and Hello Patient cover scheduling well but leave RCM workflows to staff, while Prosper AI and Parakeet Health cover broader call surfaces with different depth on the payer side.


### Is Prosper AI better than Assort Health for orthopedic practices with high prior authorization volume?


For practices running 30 or more surgical prior auths per week, Prosper AI is the stronger fit. Assort Health's scripted state machine handles scheduling-heavy orthopedic call flows well, but insurance eligibility and prior authorization were both uncovered in a 2026 field evaluation. Adding those call types after go-live requires vendor engineering rather than self-configuration.


### What should I test when assessing any AI agent for an orthopedic practice?


Call the vendor's live customer number and test three things: whether it answers an off-script payer-specific question without transferring, whether it tracks a mid-call topic change without resetting, and whether it handles a language switch mid-conversation. These tests take 10 to 15 minutes and reveal more about real-world performance than any feature list or demo environment.


### Is Prosper AI HIPAA-compliant?


Yes. Prosper AI is designed to handle protected health information across both patient-facing and payer-facing calls in a healthcare environment.
